title: Pinegrove Bank - integration call notes
content:
Attendees: Daniel Cho (Pinegrove - Head of AI), Maya Lin (Pinegrove - Platform), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Solutions), Priya Saha (Redwood PM)

High-level: 60m intro + discovery. Pinegrove is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing virtual assistant (account support + transaction search) and internal fraud triage workflows. Primary concerns: PII/security, latency for customer-facing flows, predictable cost, and ability to run in VPC/on-prem for regulated datasets. They want an initial pilot in Q3 with ~3 canonical intents and limited traffic, then scale to production by Q1 2027 if pilot goes well.

Key requirements / asks from Pinegrove:
- Authentication: must integrate with their internal auth tokens and optional SSO. They prefer our private deployment (VPC) but will consider Dedicated if timeline for private is long.
- Data handling: no raw customer PII persisted in Redwood logs. Need KMS-backed encryption and audit logs sent to their SIEM.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for production endpoints and 100-200ms median token latency target for short prompts (<=256 tokens).
- Throughput: pilot ~5 req/s peak, production target ~200 req/s with bursts to 400.
- Model behavior: want deterministic safety filters + configurable system prompts across environments. Evaluate using our evals/rollout features.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown per route, tracing hooks, and per-route dashboards are required.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity constrained; explicit requirement for canary/A-B rollouts.

Notes / gotchas from discovery:
- They currently use an on-prem data lake and have strict egress rules. Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) likely required for any PII-heavy flows. Need to confirm whether their infra team will allow outbound telemetry to Redwood console or require collector within their VPC.
- Security team will require an architecture diagram + SOC2 / penetration test artifacts. They asked if Redwood supports HSM-managed key material - yes but need to surface the integration details.
- Latency target is aggressive. We should propose a combination of small-context models, KV caching for recent conversations, and model variants pinned to low-latency optimized runtimes.
- Cost sensitivity: payments approvals are slow; show clear unit economics for token cost vs. latency tradeoffs. Use Redwood Optimize recommendations to justify quantization and batching choices.
- They asked about thread-safety for concurrent KV cache across pods - explain that runtime manages KV cache per-session and we can shard sessions to specific GPU pools in Dedicated. For Private, we need to share design doc on cache coherence.

Technical follow-ups (Aisha / Marco):
1) Prepare a short architecture options doc (2 pages) comparing Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem) for Pinegrove use-case. Emphasize security controls, telemetry flows, and time-to-prod. Due: 2026-07-14.
2) Confirm specifics with infra: does Pinegrove require air-gapped on-prem or VPC with egress? Action: Marco to send infra questionnaire. Due: 2026-07-12.
3) Provide latency/cost estimate: run a sample config (gpt-like medium latency-optimized model vs small-low-cost variant) with assumed 200 req/s ramp to 400 bursts. Include token cost and required GPU sizing for Dedicated. Due: 2026-07-16.
4) Security pack: send SOC2 summary, pen-test summary, HSM/KMS integration notes, and sample audit log format. Priya to assemble. Due: 2026-07-13.
5) Demo plan: live demo for pilot flows (account help + transaction search) using redact-on-send + prompt templates. Target demo week of 2026-07-20.
6) Add Pinegrove to our eval harness with their sample prompts (they will provide ~100 prompt pairs). Ask: Daniel to share prompt set and 3 seed examples by 2026-07-12.

Potential risks:
- Timeline: Private deployment onboarding can take 6-8 weeks depending on infra approvals. If they need faster time-to-value, propose Dedicated as an interim.
- Compliance: If audit/legal insists on no external telemetry, that will complicate our observability offering - plan a collector/forwarder option inside their VPC.
- Cost sign-off: Procurement cycles may push pilot start into late Q3. Need exec sponsor.

Decision points for Pinegrove (for next call):
- Decide on deployment mode: Private vs Dedicated for pilot (affects timeline & pricing).
- Confirm telemetry policy: allow Redwood console telemetry or require local-only logs.
- Provide sample prompt set + a list of sensitive fields to apply redact-on-send rules.

Quick wins / low effort items to send now:
- Short explainer doc: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (1 pager) + recommended starter config (model, quantization, batch size).
- Template NDA + PO process overview for procurement.
- Sample audit log JSON + example KMS setup steps.

Next meeting: propose 2026-07-21 for pilot scoping + timeline. Suggested attendees: Daniel, Maya, Pinegrove infra lead, Aisha, Marco, Priya.

Notes to self:
- Emphasize canary rollouts and safe fallback to smaller variants in deck.
- Pull recent benchmark numbers for 256-token median latency on our low-latency runtime (2026-06 perf deck).
- Coordinate with infra to draft the questionnaire before Marco sends to Pinegrove.

Actions assigned:
- Marco: infra questionnaire + initial Dedicated sizing sketch (due 7/12)
- Priya: security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, HSM docs) (due 7/13)
- Aisha: 1-pager comparison + demo plan + schedule demo (due 7/14)
- Daniel (Pinegrove): share 100 prompt pairs and list of sensitive fields (due 7/12)

End of notes.
